title: Capacity surge slicing and quarantine zones (playbook)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook defines a different approach to multi-region spare capacity: 'surge slicing' (time-sliced, micro-allocations) combined with geographically distributed 'quarantine zones' for isolation during noisy-neighbor or catastrophic events. The goal is to keep a low steady-state holdback while ensuring predictable short-term absorptive capacity for model-serving spikes and regional failures.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: infra on-call, capacity planners, SRE, release ops.
- Scope: GPU fleet allocation across primary regions (us-west1, us-central1, eu-central1, ap-southeast1) for Hosted + Dedicated workloads. Includes guidance for Private deployments when coordinated by account engineering.

Quick summary (one-line):
Target: 8–12% nominal fleet buffer distributed as: 4% fast-absorb surge-slices, 3% regional failover holdback, 1–5% strategic quarantine reserve (varies by region risk profile). Aim for RTO 15m for routing changes, RPO minimal (no data loss for stateless inference).

Assumptions and inputs used in calculations:
- Fleet snapshot (2026-11-01): total logical GPUs = 12,800 (A100-80GB equiv). We normalize H100 as 1.6x A100, L4 as 0.25x for planning math.
- Typical 30-day p95 token throughput: hosted API 420B tokens/day, Dedicated 160B tokens/day.
- Average utilization steady-state target: 72% across serving clusters (observed).
- SLA tiers: standard (best-effort), enterprise (SLA-backed, routed to dedicated pools).
- Failover target: absorbing region must cover 60% of failing region's committed baseline within 30 minutes using surge-slices + soft preemption.

Sheet: Region baseline (normalized A100-equivalents)
Columns: REGION | INSTALLED | COMMITTED_BASELINE | STEADY_UTIL_TARGET | CURRENT_SPARE | RECOMM_HOLDBACK
us-west1 | 4,500 | 3,380 | 72% | 270 | 225
us-central1 | 3,200 | 2,720 | 72% | 200 | 160
eu-central1 | 2,100 | 1,680 | 72% | 150 | 105
ap-southeast1 | 3,000 | 2,200 | 72% | 210 | 135
Notes: COMMITTED_BASELINE = expected long-running reserved workload (dedicated customers + pinned production). CURRENT_SPARE = measured average idle pool after autoscale and pre-warm. RECOMM_HOLDBACK = recommended static holdback for regional failover (3–5% of installed depending on region volatility).

Surge-slicing model (how it works):
- Define short time-slices (T=5–30 minutes) called a slice window. Each slice can allocate an ephemeral 'surge slice' from a cross-region transient pool.
- Surge slices are enforced via scheduler labels: slice_id, preemptible=true, eviction_grace=45s.
- Each region maintains a local fast-slice pool sized to absorb single-region 95th-percentile spikes for 10 minutes. Global coordination via control-plane ledger so adjacent regions don't simultaneously allocate same slice for long-tail spikes.

Example surge calculation (us-west1):
- Observed 95th spike = +410 A100-equivalents over steady baseline during 10-minute windows.
- Local fast-slice target = 0.6 * 95th = 246 (covers 60% locally, remainder pulled cross-region).
- Cross-region spill requirement = 410 - 246 = 164 -> assign to nearest absorb region(s) (us-central1 + eu-central1 if latency OK).

Quarantine zones (new concept):
- Purpose: isolate contaminated workloads (misbehaving model variants, noisy customers, software regressions) to prevent cascading capacity erosion.
- Implementation: logical quarantine zone = a named subset of GPUs tagged with quarantine=true, network ACLs tightened, and routing policy set to `quarantine-route` for affected routes.
- Size guidance: small active quarantine pool (1% fleet) always on; latent quarantine cold pool (2–4%) can be warmed within 20–60 minutes.
- Activation triggers: automated anomaly score > 0.85 for token cost bump or continuous 50% error rate for 10 minutes; manual activation by on-call.

Soft-failover and preemption policy:
- Prioritize graceful eviction: send pre-eviction notice to running containers (45s), flush KV caches where feasible.
- Soft lanes: mark routes with priority tags (enterprise-high, enterprise-medium, hosted-beta, hosted-low). Preemption order: hosted-low -> hosted-beta -> enterprise-medium -> enterprise-high.
- Fallback images: For enterprise-high, prepare smaller quantized variants (Q4_K) to spin in as last-resort fallback to preserve throughput.

Routing handoff timeline (target when region X fails):
- 0–1m: health detection + circuit breaker trips for region X.
- 1–5m: Traffic reweighted to local holdbacks + surge-slices. DNS TTLs lowered preemptively; BGP/PSLB rebalancing if used.
- 5–15m: Cross-region allocations fully active; quarantine zones may be used to soak temporary test traffic.
- 15–60m: Autoscale and cold-pool warms finish; if capacity still short, initiate forced preemption of lower-priority routes.

Contingency allocations (prioritized order):
1) Local holdback (RECOMM_HOLDBACK) — immediate, non-evictable for SLA routes.
2) Fast-slice local pool — ephemeral short windows.
3) Cross-region absorb slices — coordinate via control plane ledger.
4) Quarantine cold pool warm -> used for non-critical traffic.
5) Forced preemption of hosted-low and hosted-beta.

Simulation excerpt (table of synthetic scenarios run on 2026-10-28):
Scenario A: us-west1 partial outage (30% of nodes degraded)
- Needed absorb capacity = 1,200 A100-eq
- Available local holdback + fast-slices = 640
- Cross-region absorb available = 580
- Result: routing change within 7m, forced preemption not needed, SLA impact within alert thresholds.

Scenario B: eu-central1 total zone fail during peak EU morning
- Needed absorb capacity = 1,700
- Available local + fast-slices = 420
- Cross-region absorb = 1,100 (us-central1 + us-west1 split)
- Quarantine cold pool warmed -> +120
- Result: partial soft-degradation of non-enterprise routes for 18m, enterprise routes sustained by pre-warmed quantized fallbacks.

Operational runbook (quick play):
- Detect: Pager on call (SRE) receives alert: regional health > 90% degraded or p95 latency > 2x baseline.
- Assess: Run capacity-check script (ops/bin/surge-assess) -> outputs per-region absorb shortfall and recommended preemption sets.
- Act: On-call modifies policy via console: toggle cross-region-absorber = on; enable quarantine-route for affected model groups; increase control-plane slice window to 30m if noise persists.
- Communicate: Post incident stub to #infra-incident with short summary, affected customers, actions taken.
- Postmortem: Owner assigned within 72h; include metrics: time-to-route-change, peak preemption count, SLA error minutes.

Metrics to track (KPIs):
- Time to routing reweight (target < 15m)
- Percentage of spikes absorbed without forced preemption (> 90%)
- Quarantine activations per quarter (trend down)
- Cross-region allocation conflicts (should be < 2 per 1,000 allocations)
- Cost delta during incidents (tokens/$) compared to baseline

Implementation notes / technical constraints:
- Scheduler: Require support for eviction_grace and preemptible labels; tie into autoscaler to enforce slice duration.
- Control plane ledger: canonical small datastore with per-slice locks to avoid double allocation; TTL for locks 45s + safety margin.
- Telemetry: add slice_id to traces and per-token cost logs to enable chargeback for cross-region absorb events.
- Security: quarantine zones must be KMS-isolated for private deployments where customer data is concerned; coordinate with security team for certs.

Risks and open questions:
- Latency cost: cross-region absorb increases p95 for routed requests — acceptable for hosted-low but needs enterprise opt-outs.
- Quarantine sizing: how to pick 1–5% for long tail? Proposed approach: use 12 months of contamination events to compute 90th percentile impact and size latent pool accordingly.
- Billing and cost attribution: when we absorb dedicated customers cross-region, who pays for burst costs? Need billing policy (linked ticket JIRA-INFRA-941).

Action items (next 6 weeks):
- [ ] Prototype control-plane ledger for slices (owner: Liam) — due 2026-11-22.
- [ ] Add slice_id in telemetry traces and cost logs (owner: Priya) — due 2026-11-29.
- [ ] Run 3 chaos experiments simulating regional fail + noisy neighbor to validate quarantine warming (owner: Samuel) — due 2026-12-10.
- [ ] Draft billing opt-in policy for enterprise customers that require cross-region absorption (owner: Maya) — due 2026-12-03.

Appendix A: short glossary:
- Surge-slice: ephemeral allocation window used to absorb short spikes.
- Quarantine zone: tagged subset of GPUs reserved for isolating misbehaving workloads.
- Fast-slice: local, short-duration slice optimized for low latency.
- Cold pool: dormant capacity that requires warm-up (20–60m).

Appendix B: useful commands (ops):
- ops/bin/surge-assess --region us-west1 --window 10m
- ops/bin/ledger-lock --slice-id S-20261105-01 --acquire
- ops/bin/activate-quarantine --zone eu-central1 --size 120

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc proposes operational semantics (surge-slicing + quarantine) that are intentionally different from traditional static reserves. Looking for feedback on preemption ordering, quarantine sizing, and cross-region billing policies.
